source_claims.statement: Systematic exploration of Z-Push ActiveSync. Multiple SQLi attempts in URL params, POST, XML, headers, different SQL dialects produced consistent response times and no errors.
Shifted to authentication mechanism; injected into username of Basic Auth header. Timing with sleep confirmed (8s for 5s sleep).

research_questions.formulation: After standard parameter and body injection points show no differential behavior, does the authentication username field reach the database?
research_questions.anchor: pivot to Basic Auth username after other vectors failed
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether auth credentials are used in SQL
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that auth fields are handled separately from injectable parameters

environment_model_updates: Z-Push 2.4.4+0 ActiveSync server with PostgreSQL backend
Authentication required; baseline response times stable

systematic_vs_exploratory.systematic: endpoint probing, testing common SQLi locations and dialects
systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: moving to authentication username after standard locations failed

negative_inconclusive: URL params, POST, XML, headers, multiple SQL syntaxes: consistent times, no errors (bounded negatives)
unobserved_history: exact list of tested payloads before the auth pivot
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat early consistent timings as proof of no SQLi
Auth username injection is a distinct surface from request parameters
layer_b_candidate_principles: When common injection surfaces show no differential behavior, test authentication fields (username, password) before concluding the application is not injectable
Stable baseline timings make sleep-based confirmation reliable once a candidate surface is identified
model_vs_harness: Choosing to test auth fields after other vectors fail is model judgment; systematic testing of parameters and timing measurement can be harness.
